parsed.notes: Lens A reviewed support, existence, and disclosed-field consistency only; no treatment/currency defect is asserted.

reasons: The lake record identifies the case as United States v. Knights, decided by the U.S. Supreme Court on 2001-12-10, year 2001.
The lake citations list official cite 534 U.S. 112, parallels 122 S. Ct. 587 and 151 L. Ed. 2d 497, and vendor-neutral cite 2001 U.S. LEXIS 10950.

The opinion directly addresses Griffin's special-needs probation-search rationale and rejects the Ninth Circuit's view that only a Griffin-like special-needs search could satisfy the Fourth Amendment.

The opinion states that the search was reasonable under the Court's general Fourth Amendment approach, making the case a refinement of the special-needs/probation-search line rather than a pure special-needs holding.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not include a separate taxonomy defining the editorial word Key, so this stands as a support judgment from the opinion's central doctrinal treatment.

defect.evidence_quote: We therefore hold that the warrantless search of Knights, supported by reasonable suspicion and authorized by a condition of probation, was reasonable within the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.
defect.problem: The holding is substantively supported, but the frontmatter assertion is truncated at 'under the Fourth…' and should state the complete Fourth Amendment formulation.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the holding with: A warrantless search of a probationer's residence, supported by reasonable suspicion and authorized by a probation search condition, is reasonable within the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.

reasons: The opinion supports the reasonable-suspicion probation-search rule and final holding.
The opinion also expressly reserves suspicionless searches, so the holding should remain tied to reasonable suspicion and a probation search condition.
residual_risks: Do not extend the rule to suspicionless searches or probationers lacking a search condition.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the opinion's own limits: probationer, search condition, reasonable suspicion, and Fourth Amendment reasonableness.

reasons: The lake identity fields list court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus, supporting the page's Binding — SCOTUS weight label.
No treatment-currency finding is raised under Lens A.

The page treatment fields match the lake treatment judgment fields: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 2001-12-10, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, composite_basis migration-seed, composite_basis_ref United States v. Knights, and varies_by_point false.
Treatment and currency are outside Lens A, so this is only a disclosed-field consistency verdict.
